body.translated_text:
<s>Ālambanaparīkṣāvṛtti</s> (Commentary on the Examination of the Objective Support)
Composed by <s>Ācārya Dignāga</s>
Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: ye cakṣurādijñānasyālambanaṃ bāhyārtho 'stītīcchanti / nanu te kalpayanti paramāṇun; tatkāraṇātvāt[jñānasya] / saṃghātaṃ vā tadābhajñānasya jāyamānatvāt / tatra tāvat
body.translated_text: Those who assert that an external object is the <s>ālambana</s> (objective support) of visual and other cognitions—they postulate either atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>), because they are the cause [of cognition]; or an aggregate (<s>saṃghāta</s>), because cognition having its form arises [from it]. Regarding the first:

children.translated_text: Even though the graspable aspect (= atoms) may be the cause of sense-cognition,

children.text: atadābhatayā tasyā nākṣavadviṣayaḥ sa tu(aṇavaḥ) // Āv_1 //
children.translated_text: because [cognition] does not bear their form, they are not its object, like the sense-faculty. // 1 //

body.text: viṣaya iti / jñānena svarūpa meva nirdhāryate / tadākāratayā jāyamānatvāt / yadyapyaṇavaḥ tatkāraṇam / tathāpi na tādṛśāḥ akṣavat / evañca nāṇavastāvadālambanam / saṃghātastu tadābhatve 'pi[jñānamya nālambanam / yataḥ]
body.translated_text: 'Object' means: its own nature is ascertained by cognition, because [cognition] arises bearing its form. Even if atoms are the cause of cognition, still they are not [its object] of that character, like the sense-faculty. Thus, atoms are not the <s>ālambana</s>. As for the aggregate, even though [cognition] bears its form, [it is not the ālambana, because:]
That of which it bears the appearance is not its [cause]—

body.text: yo 'rthaḥ svāvabhāsivijñaptimutpādayati sahyālambanaṃ yujyate / yataḥ sa eva hyutpattipratyaya ucyate / saṃghātastu naivam /
body.translated_text: That object which produces a cognition bearing its own appearance is properly the <s>ālambana</s>, since that alone is called the generative condition (<s>utpattipratyaya</s>). But the aggregate is not so.
Because of the absence of [real] substance, like [the perception of] a double moon.

body.text: indriyavaikalyāt dvicandradarśanasya tadābhatve 'pi na tasya viṣayo 'sti / tadvat saṃghātaḥ dravyato 'sattvena akāraṇātvāt nālambanam /
body.translated_text: The perception of a double moon, due to a defect of the sense-organ, even though it bears that appearance, has no [real] object. Likewise, the aggregate, being non-existent as a [real] substance and hence not a cause, is not the <s>ālambana</s>.

body.text: evaṃ bāhyadūyañcaiva na yuktaṃ matigocaraḥ // Āv_2 //
body.translated_text: Thus, neither of the two external [candidates] is properly the domain of cognition. // 2 //

body.text: aṇuḥ kalāpaśceti bāhyo 'rthaḥ nālambanam, ekāṅgavaikalyāt // tatra sādhanaṃ sañcitākāramicchanti kila kecana /
body.translated_text: The atom and the aggregate as external objects are not the <s>ālambana</s>, due to the deficiency of one condition in each. // Therein, some assert the composite form as the proof:

body.text:
sarvo 'rtho bahvākāraḥ ataḥ tatra kenacidākāreṇa pratyakṣa ipyate /
paramāṇuṣvapyasti sañcitābhajñānotpattikāraṇabhāvaḥ /
body.translated_text:
Every object has many aspects; therefore, through some [particular] aspect it is directly perceived.
Even in atoms there exists the capacity to cause the arising of cognition bearing the composite appearance.
The atomic form is not the object of cognition, like hardness and the like. // 3 //

body.text: yathā kaṭhinatādi vidyamānamapi na cākṣuṣabuddhiviṣayaḥ / evamanutvamapi //
body.translated_text: Just as hardness and the like, though present [in objects], are not the object of visual cognition, so too is atomic nature [not its object].
If that were so, then the cognition of a pot, a dish, and so forth would be the same.
Among the atoms of a pot, dish, and the like, even though many, there is no difference whatsoever.
If difference [of cognition] is due to difference of form—

body.text: yadi manyase grīvādyākāraḥ viśeṣakriyā yena buddherviśeṣaṇamupādhirbhavet / iti / ayamupādhirdhaṭādāvasti /
body.translated_text: if you think that the form of a neck and so forth is a distinguishing property (<s>upādhi</s>) that serves as a qualifier making the cognition specific—this qualifier exists in pots and the like,
but does not exist in atoms that are truly real substances. // 4 //
Because of the absence of a difference in the means of valid cognition—
among atoms and other [real] substances, there is no difference in their spherical nature (<s>pārimaṇḍalya</s>).
It exists in what is not a [real] substance; therefore, it [the form-difference] belongs to that.

body.text: ākārabhedaḥ saṃvṛtisatsvevāsti na tu paramāṇuṣu / ghaṭādayaśca saṃvṛtisanta eva //
body.translated_text: Difference of form exists only in things that are conventionally real (<s>saṃvṛtisat</s>), not in atoms. And pots and the like are only conventionally real.
For when atoms are excluded, cognition bearing that form collapses. // 5 //

body.text: dravyasatsu apanītasambandhiṣvapi[nīla-] varṇādivat svabuddhirna tyajyate / tathā sati indriyabuddhīnāṃ viṣayo bahirnāstītyupapadyate //
body.translated_text: When truly real substances have their relations removed, still, like blue color and the like, the cognition of them is not relinquished. This being so, it is established that there is no external object as the domain of sense-cognitions.
But that which has the internal form of what is to be grasped, yet appears as if external—
that is the [true] object.
When no external object exists, the internal [form] that appears as if external is the <s>ālambana-pratyaya</s> (objective condition).
Because it is of the nature of cognition, and also because it is a condition of that [cognition]. // 6 //

body.text: antarvijñāna marthatayāvabhāsate tato utpadyate ceti dharmatādvayaviśiṣṭamityataḥ antassadevālambanapratyayaḥ //
body.translated_text: The internal cognition appears as an object—from it [cognition] arises—being qualified by this twofold characteristic, therefore only the internal [form] is the <s>ālambana-pratyaya</s>.

body.text: yadi tāvadevamavabhāsa eva vedyate / kathaṃ tadekadeśaḥ sahajātaḥ pratyayaḥ /
body.translated_text: If indeed only the appearance is what is cognized, how can a co-arisen [element] be a condition of a part of it?
One part is a condition [of the other] because of non-deviation—

body.text: sahabhūto 'pi avyabhicārāt anyajātasya pratyayo bhavatī // naiyāyikāstu evamāhuḥ / krameṇa jāyamānayorhetuhetumatoḥ bhavābhāvatadvattā lakṣaṇa miti // athavā
body.translated_text: even a simultaneous [element], because of its invariable concomitance, can be a condition of something of another kind. // The <s>Naiyāyikas</s>, however, say this: the defining characteristic of cause and effect, which arise successively, is the presence or absence of the [cause] and [the consequent] possession or non-possession of the [effect]. // Alternatively,
because of the bestowal of potency, or successively.

body.text: krameṇāpi so 'rthāvabhāsaḥ svānurūpakāryotpattaye śaktiṃ vijñānadhārāṃ karotītyavirodhaḥ // yadi tarhi svarūpamevālambanapratyayaḥ / kathaṃ tat[rūpaṃ] cakṣuścopādāya cakṣurvijñānamutpadyate // [iti] /
body.translated_text: Even successively, that appearance of the object imparts a potency to the stream of consciousness for producing an effect conforming to itself—thus there is no contradiction. // If, then, the own-nature itself is the <s>ālambana-pratyaya</s>, how does visual consciousness arise depending on the eye and that [form]? //
What is of the nature of a potency through the force of cooperative conditions—that is the sense-faculty. // 7 //

body.text: indriyaṃ svakāryāt śaktirūpamevānumīyate na tu bhautikam /
body.translated_text: The sense-faculty is inferred from its own effect as being merely of the nature of a potency, not as material (<s>bhautika</s>).
And that [potency] is not contradictory to cognition—

body.text: śaktistu vijñāne vāstu / anirdeśye svasya rūpe vāstu kāryotpattau na viśeṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: the potency may reside in consciousness, or it may reside in its own indescribable form—in the production of effects there is no difference.
Thus, that which has the form of an object,
and the potency, each being the cause of the other, has been operating from beginningless time. // 8 //

body.text: cakṣurākhyāṃ śaktimantaḥ rūpañcopādāya vijñānamarthāvabhāsi ālambanādavibhaktamutpadyate / idaṃ dvayamapi anādikālamanyonyahetukam / kadācit vijñānasya śaktiparipākāt viṣayākāratā bhavati / kadācicca tadākāraśaktiḥ / vijñānaṃ sā ca ubhayamanyatvenānanyatvena ca yatheṣṭamucyatām / evamantarālambanaṃ dharmatādvayaviśiṣṭatvāt viṣayatayā upapadyate //
body.translated_text: Having internally the capacity called 'eye' and taking on form, consciousness — appearing as an object — arises undivided from the <s>ālambana</s> (object-support). This pair too has been mutually causal since beginningless time. Sometimes, from the maturation of consciousness's capacity, the aspect of the object arises. And sometimes, the capacity for that aspect [arises from the object]. Let consciousness and that [capacity] — these two — be spoken of as different or non-different, as one wishes. Thus, the internal <s>ālambana</s> (object), being qualified by the two properties (<s>dharmatādvaya</s>), is established as the [proper] object of cognition.
Thus ends the <s>Ālambanaparīkṣāvṛtti</s> (Commentary on the Examination of the Object of Cognition), composed by the master <s>Dignāga</s>.
